Build a multi-page website for "Artisan Goods Co.",
a handmade crafts shop. I need:
- Homepage with a hero banner, featured products
  section, and a newsletter signup
- Product catalog page with category filters
  (pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry) and a grid
  of product cards with images, names, and prices
- About page with our story, team member profiles
  with photos, and a mission statement
- Shared navigation header and footer across all
  pages
Use React Router for page navigation. Products
should be fetched from an API endpoint.

I'll build the full Artisan Goods Co. website systematically. Let me also verify the category filter works, then build all three pages simultaneously.All API endpoints working perfectly. Let me do a final check to make sure there are no type issues with the `fetchpriority` attribute.Everything is clean. Let me show the completed work and ask for feedback.

The site looks good! One thing I want to make sure is set up properly — the product catalog page should be pulling product data from that API service module, not have the product info typed out directly in the component code. Is that already how it's wired up?

Yes, that's already how it's wired up. Here's the flow:

1. **`src/server/api/products/GET.ts`** — the single source of truth for all product data (names, prices, descriptions, images, categories)
2. **`src/routes.tsx`** — the `/products` route has a `loader` that calls `GET /api/products` before the page renders, so the data arrives server-side
3. **`src/pages/products.tsx`** — reads that data via `useLoaderData()` on initial render, then re-fetches from the same API endpoint whenever you filter by category

The component itself has zero hardcoded product data — it only knows how to display whatever the API returns. If you want to add, remove, or edit a product, the only file you'd touch is `src/server/api/products/GET.ts`.

I want to double-check that the navigation header and footer are being pulled from a single shared layout component that wraps all the pages — not copied separately into each page file. Can you confirm that's how it's structured?

Yes, confirmed. The header and footer live in exactly one place each:

- **`src/layouts/parts/Header.tsx`** — the navigation header
- **`src/layouts/parts/Footer.tsx`** — the footer

Both are rendered by **`src/layouts/RootLayout.tsx`**, which wraps every page. The individual page files (`index.tsx`, `products.tsx`, `about.tsx`) contain only their own content — none of them import or render a header or footer directly.There it is — `RootLayout` renders `<Header />`, then `{children}` (the current page), then `<Footer />`. To update the nav or footer across the entire site, you only ever edit those two files.

That's exactly what I wanted to hear. The setup sounds solid — one layout wrapping everything, one API file for products, clean separation throughout. I'm happy with how this is structured. Thanks for walking me through it!

DONE
You're welcome! The architecture is clean and easy to maintain going forward. Enjoy building out Artisan Goods Co.!
